title: Positive-angle quotient bounded by Gaussian surface area
statement: Let $n\ge 0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $\delta>0$. Then $\sqrt{\pi/2}\,s_A(\delta)/\delta\le P_\gamma(A)$, where $s_A(\delta)$ is the rotation sensitivity of $A$ and $P_\gamma(A)$ is its Gaussian surface area defined by the lower limit of the positive-angle quotients.
replaced: Let $n\ge0$, let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $G,G\prime$ be independent vectors with law $\gamma_n$. Write $s_A(t)$ for the real value of the product-measure mass $(\gamma_n\otimes\gamma_n)\{(g,h):\mathbf1_A(g)\ne\mathbf1_A(\cos t\,g+\sin t\,h)\}$. Write $P_\gamma(A)=\liminf_{t\to0^+}\bigl[\sqrt{\pi/2}\,s_A(t)/t\bigr]_+$ in $[0,\infty]$, where $[x]_+=\max(x,0)$. If $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is measurable and $\delta>0$, then $[\sqrt{\pi/2}\,s_A(\delta)/\delta]_+\le P_\gamma(A)$.
